content.comment_body: Hello, I'm a bit confused! 1) My measuring range is 0 to 6 bar, but in the software settings it shows 0 to 6000. 2) When do we actually need to use an amplifier for analog inputs? Is it always necessary? Best regards, [user_name]

Hello [user_name], welcome to the forum. The analog/digital converter in an analog input of [product_name] generally converts any analog signal (such as 0-10V, 0/4-20mA, PT100/1000) into a scale ranging from 0-1000 units. You'll need the analog amplifier to set your sensor's physical measurement range. This lets you display values like 0-6000 (as in your example) as 0-6000 mbar, or as 0.000-6.000 bar with three decimal places.

Thank you very much [user_name]. I'm new to [product_name]. When do we select 'no sensor' in the analog amplifier settings? Is it possible to use 'no sensor' after the analog input block? Best regards, [user_name]
The simplest and most effective way to learn is by testing in simulation. Set your required configurations and then switch to 'No sensor' to observe its impact (or lack thereof).

analysis.insight_summary: Users express uncertainty about configuring measuring ranges and understanding when an analog amplifier is needed for analog inputs in [product_name]. It's not immediately clear to newcomers how the analog amplifier influences mapping of sensor values, and when to utilize the 'no sensor' option. Simulation and testing are suggested as effective methods for gaining practical understanding.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want clear explanations about when it is necessary to use an analog amplifier and how to correlate software values with physical sensor ranges in [product_name]. Additionally, there is a desire to know in which cases selecting the 'no sensor' option is appropriate.
pain_keywords: unclear mapping of physical to software values
